t.E161g.agn: In 2010 EFSA set the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 0.03 mg/kg body weight because crystal deposits were observed in the retina of the eye in humans and monkeys. It reported that total intake from food and feed is not expected to exceed this limit.
t.E161g.body: In rats, canthaxanthin accumulates in fatty tissue, the liver and the spleen; it is eliminated very slowly from fatty tissue, and its levels in other tissues fall within weeks after intake stops.
t.E161g.eff.0.a: Well above the daily limit; the amount taken in from food is not expected to exceed this limit
t.E161g.eff.0.t: Crystal deposits have been observed in the retina of the eye; the daily limit is based on this finding
t.E161g.eval: Colour. In the EU it is authorised in food only in Strasbourg sausage (saucisse de Strasbourg); EFSA set the ADI at 0.03 mg/kg and reported that intake is unlikely to exceed this value.
t.E161g.found.0: In the EU, only Strasbourg sausage
t.E161g.prod: Produced by chemical synthesis; a carotenoid that also occurs in nature.
t.E161g.summary: An orange-red carotenoid. In the EU it is authorised in food only in Strasbourg sausage; also used in animal feed.
